claim: Eflornithine might be a novel therapy for patients with Bachmann-Bupp syndrome.
source: Based on previously published murine data with eflornithine for gain-of-function variants (Soler et al., 1996), multiple long-term safety studies for clinical use in African sleeping sickness (trypanosomiasis), colorectal cancer, and neuroblastoma (Alirol et al., 2013; Priotto et al., 2009; Saulnier Sholler et al., 2015; Meyskens et al., 2008), and the absense of toxicity in the patient's primary cell culture inresponse to eflornithine (Schultz et al., 2019), we surmised eflornithine might be a novel therapy for patients with this syndrome.
